Bahrain Oil & Gas Output Hit as Respiratory Virus Spreads Among Workers

A respiratory virus outbreak among workers has disrupted operations in Bahrain’s Oil & Gas Producers industry, leading to significant reductions in output and raising concerns over the stability of near-term supply commitments. The outbreak, first detected last week at the East Sitra Processing Complex, has since been reported at three further sites, according to the Bahrain Hydrocarbon Producers Association (BHPA).

Over 320 workers have tested positive for the newly identified virus, which local health officials describe as “highly transmissible in close-quarters environments common to energy production facilities.” Several sites, including the South Hidd Refinery operated by Gulf Trident Petroleum, have moved to skeleton staffing after a surge in confirmed cases forced the quarantine of entire shifts.

“Production at our affected facilities is currently running at 40-50% capacity,” said Latif Al-Hasan, Chief Operations Officer at Gulf Trident Petroleum, in a statement on Tuesday. “We are working closely with health authorities to contain the outbreak and safeguard our workforce, but the situation remains dynamic.”

The BHPA estimates that, as of Tuesday morning, aggregate crude output in Bahrain has declined by approximately 18% compared to the average of the preceding month. With more than 800 industry staff now placed under isolation protocols, the association warned that further operational disruptions could occur if the outbreak is not contained in the coming days.

Logistics have also been impacted, with a union representative reporting delays in the transportation of both personnel and essential materials. “Many of our members are unable to report for duty or have been placed in quarantine accommodation,” said Fatima Khalil, spokesperson for the Bahrain Oil Workers Union. “Maintenance routines are being deferred and this raises safety concerns for aging infrastructure.”

The Ministry of Oil and Environment has deployed rapid response medical teams to affected sites and introduced mandatory daily health screenings. Officials say they are closely monitoring the situation but caution that the full impact will depend on the speed of containment. “We are prioritizing health and safety, but we recognize that ongoing disruptions could affect short-term export volumes,” a ministry spokesperson told local media.

Industry analysts say the outbreak comes at a sensitive time for Bahrain’s energy sector, which has been seeking to ramp up production following recent investment in upstream projects. “Any prolonged reduction in output could ripple through contractual supply obligations,” said Yusef Mansouri, regional energy analyst at Al-Muqaddim Financial.

At the time of writing, the outbreak remains active, with further updates expected as containment efforts continue.
